findings.claim: The QA route drives the one-paragraph hands-on instructions beginning at html-css-js/html-and-css/grid/artifact.html:248, but neither the route nor the artifact presents each task as numbered where-to-look, what-to-type-or-press, what-to-expect, and how-to-know-done steps. The current route can therefore pass while the captain-required instruction shape is absent.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite each hands-on task as an accessible numbered list with explicit where, action, expected result, and done criterion, without exposing the reasoning answer; update the QA path to assert that structure while retaining the same behavioral route.

findings.claim: The manifest records modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.50 minutes, while the review direction fixes this module route at modeledP50 + 2.0. The result is conservative and remains under 15 minutes, but it does not use the required model.
findings.recommendation: Recalculate modeledWorstPath as modeledP50 + 2.0, update the basis text, and derive budget/aboutLabel from that corrected value without exceeding the 15-minute ceiling.

findings.claim: The Grid-versus-Flexbox rule equates one-dimensional Flexbox with “a single row or column” and “one line,” yet the page’s own sorter recommends Flexbox for tags that wrap. Flexbox remains one-dimensional when wrapping because each flex line is laid out independently; it is not limited to a single physical line.

evidence.section: 1.1 Overview and 9.7 Resolving Flexible Lengths: multi-line flex containers remain one-dimensional; free-space resolution uses outer hypothetical main sizes, constraints and scaled shrink factors

findings.recommendation: Replace “single row or column/one line” with “one dimension at a time; wrapped lines are independent and do not align as shared columns.” Preserve Grid as the choice when cross-row and cross-column alignment is required.
